record.title: England’s explicit non-excused overseas-departure prohibition, including Channel Tunnel travel
record.scope: England-only outbound legal prohibition; rail/tunnel component retained in this land-focused register
record.crossings: International rail/tunnel departures from England, including Folkestone and international passenger rail terminals
record.movement: Persons leaving England for overseas destinations without a reasonable excuse.
record.exceptions: Reasonable excuses including work and other listed needs; specified hauliers, tunnel workers and other transport/diplomatic categories exempt.
record.imposing_authority: UK Secretary of State for England; police and designated enforcement officers
record.enforcement: Criminal prohibition and directions available; no claim that the tunnel physically closed.
record.consequences: Non-excused overseas departures unlawful during this legal phase.
record.relationship: Distinct from French-side EU028 and R3-EU-010 restrictions on UK arrivals.
record.status_observation: Historical evidence only; not a present-day status assessment
record.official_rationale: Respond to the COVID-19 public-health threat.
record.context: Specific Regulation 8 phase replaced the earlier lockdown framework; this is not a claim that holiday travel first became restricted on 29 March.
record.uncertainty: Formal repeal does not establish first actual leisure train movement. England application must not be generalized to all UK jurisdictions or Northern Ireland’s land border.

historical.duration_note: Formal permission or repeal; operational continuity and first physical reopening are not established. Legal phase only; no uniform observed rail-user closure interval is claimed.
